questions: Did the swelling and redness start suddenly within the last 24 hours?
Are you having any trouble breathing, swallowing, or speaking?
Do you feel swelling of your lips, tongue, or throat?
Do you have hives or an itchy rash anywhere else on your body?
Have you recently eaten a new food, taken a new medication, or been exposed to a new cosmetic, chemical, or insect sting?
Is the affected area painful or tender?
Is the skin warm to the touch?
Has the redness or swelling been rapidly spreading?
Do you have pain with moving either eye?
Has your vision become blurry or doubled?
Have you had an injury, bite, or wound to your face recently?
Have you had similar episodes before?
orders: Focused skin examination for heliotrope rash, Gottron papules, shawl-sign erythema, nailfold changes, and poikiloderma
Manual muscle-strength examination of the neck flexors and proximal upper- and lower-extremity muscles
Serum creatine kinase, aldolase, AST, ALT, and LDH
Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, urinalysis, ESR, and CRP
ANA by immunofluorescence and a myositis-specific antibody panel
Dermatology examination with a punch biopsy of the affected skin
MRI of the proximal muscles with T2/STIR sequences

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis (cutaneous dermatomyositis without muscle involvement), presumed idiopathic autoimmune

ALTERNATIVE: Morbihan disease (persistent rosacea-associated facial edema)

ALTERNATIVE: Cutaneous lupus erythematosus

ALTERNATIVE: Chronic bilateral periorbital dermatitis/angioedema of noninfectious origin
